walkthroughs.body_html: Oceans 97 percent; ice 2 percent; groundwater 0.6 percent; surface fresh water (rivers, lakes) 0.3 percent; atmosphere 0.001 percent. Of fresh water only, 69 percent is in ice. Fresh available liquid water (rivers, lakes, accessible groundwater) is just 0.7 percent of all water.

Global evaporation ~500000 km^3/yr; precipitation balances over years. Oceans evaporate 425000 km^3/yr; receive only 385000 km^3/yr from precipitation. The 40000 km^3 difference flows back as runoff from land. Powers global atmospheric circulation.

Atmospheric vapour 9 days; rivers 16 days; soils weeks-months; lakes years; groundwater 100-10000 years; ice sheets 100000 years; oceans 3200 years. Shorter residence means greater sensitivity to disturbance.

mcqs.q: How do humans affect the carbon cycle?
options: By burning fossil fuels (releasing stored geological carbon to the atmosphere) and deforestation (reducing the biosphere store and releasing carbon).
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
Humans only affect the carbon cycle by breathing out CO2.
It is only water evaporating from puddles and lakes.
The combined loss of water from a surface through evaporation (from soil and water bodies) and transpiration (from plant leaves).
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.
Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
